architecture: Mobile Banking App — first-draft proposal (as submitted by engineering, pre-review)

findings.threat: A compromised payment-service container/process could use its Contributor role to read, modify, or delete ANY resource in the subscription — not just the ones it actually needs.
findings.impact: Full subscription compromise from a single workload breach.
findings.policy: payment-service may hold only a purpose-scoped custom role, never Owner/Contributor.
findings.mitigation: Replace with a custom role scoped to exactly the resource(s) payment-service needs (see modules/iam's custom role_definition pattern).

findings.threat: A compromised account-service container/process could use its Contributor role to read, modify, or delete ANY resource in the subscription — not just the ones it actually needs.
findings.impact: Full subscription compromise from a single workload breach.
findings.policy: account-service may hold only a purpose-scoped custom role, never Owner/Contributor.
findings.mitigation: Replace with a custom role scoped to exactly the resource(s) account-service needs (see modules/iam's custom role_definition pattern).

findings.threat: customer-db is reachable directly from the internet, bypassing every network control.
findings.impact: Direct exposure of customer data to internet-wide scanning and exploitation.
findings.policy: customer-db must disable public network access and be reachable only via private endpoint.
findings.mitigation: Set public_network_access_enabled = false and add a private endpoint in the data subnet.

findings.threat: customer-storage is reachable directly from the internet, bypassing every network control.
findings.impact: Direct exposure of customer data to internet-wide scanning and exploitation.
findings.policy: customer-storage must disable public network access and be reachable only via private endpoint.
findings.mitigation: Set public_network_access_enabled = false and add a private endpoint in the data subnet.

findings.threat: Any container in customer-storage could be individually set to public, exposing its contents with a URL.
findings.impact: Silent data exposure — no network log will show it as unusual, it's 'working as configured'.
findings.mitigation: Disable public nested-item access at the account level so no container can opt in later.

findings.finding: No network segmentation in trust boundary 'flat'
findings.threat: Compute workloads and sensitive data stores share one flat network zone. A single compromised container can reach every data store here directly — this is the exact 'payment service → unrestricted database access' pattern.
findings.impact: Lateral movement from any one compromised service to all sensitive data.
findings.policy: Compute and sensitive-data tiers must sit in separate subnets with NSGs restricting cross-tier traffic to the minimum required.
findings.mitigation: Split into dedicated subnets (see modules/network's gateway/aks/data/mgmt layout) with deny-by-default NSGs.

findings.finding: customer-db has no encryption at rest
findings.threat: Data in customer-db is readable/tamperable by anyone with disk-level or backup access.
findings.impact: Regulatory exposure (data protection requirements) plus tampering risk on backups/snapshots.
findings.policy: customer-db must have infrastructure/double encryption enabled.
findings.mitigation: Enable encryption at rest (see the require-encryption-at-rest Azure Policy in modules/policy).

findings.finding: customer-storage has no encryption at rest
findings.threat: Data in customer-storage is readable/tamperable by anyone with disk-level or backup access.
findings.impact: Regulatory exposure (data protection requirements) plus tampering risk on backups/snapshots.
findings.policy: customer-storage must have infrastructure/double encryption enabled.
findings.mitigation: Enable encryption at rest (see the require-encryption-at-rest Azure Policy in modules/policy).

findings.threat: Without diagnostic logs flowing to a central workspace, there's no way to reconstruct what happened after an incident, or prove who did what.
findings.impact: Undetectable breaches and no forensic trail — also a compliance gap (most frameworks require audit logging).
findings.policy: All resources must send diagnostic logs to a central Log Analytics workspace.
findings.mitigation: Wire up diagnostic settings + a Log Analytics workspace (Phase 9 — SIEM + Detection, not yet built).

findings.threat: notification-service reaches sensitive data with no assigned identity. In practice this gets worked around with a shared service account, an ambient credential, or a manually-granted broad role — all worse than a scoped one from the start.
findings.impact: No way to attribute or limit this workload's access; likely over-privileged in practice.
findings.policy: notification-service must have its own purpose-scoped identity before going live.
findings.mitigation: Create a dedicated app registration/service principal and custom role for notification-service, matching payment-service's pattern.

findings.threat: Network reachability from api-gateway to payment-service exists, but there's no app-layer proof of identity (mTLS/OAuth/service-mesh token) — anything else that lands in the same subnet can impersonate the caller.
findings.impact: Any workload placed in the same network path can call this service as if it were the legitimate caller.
findings.policy: Traffic into payment-service must be mutually authenticated, not just network-reachable.
findings.mitigation: Introduce a service mesh (mTLS) or OAuth token validation between gateway and services (Phase 4 — Zero Trust).

findings.threat: Network reachability from api-gateway to account-service exists, but there's no app-layer proof of identity (mTLS/OAuth/service-mesh token) — anything else that lands in the same subnet can impersonate the caller.
findings.impact: Any workload placed in the same network path can call this service as if it were the legitimate caller.
findings.policy: Traffic into account-service must be mutually authenticated, not just network-reachable.
findings.mitigation: Introduce a service mesh (mTLS) or OAuth token validation between gateway and services (Phase 4 — Zero Trust).

findings.finding: api-gateway has no WAF/rate-limiting in front of it
findings.threat: api-gateway is directly internet-facing with no layer-7 filtering — vulnerable to L7 DoS and common injection patterns hitting the app directly.
findings.impact: Availability risk and a missing layer of defense against common web attacks.
findings.policy: api-gateway must sit behind a WAF (Azure Application Gateway/Front Door WAF policy).
findings.mitigation: Deploy Azure Front Door or Application Gateway with a WAF policy in front of the gateway subnet.
